repostWarningTravels.title: Serial re-posters are now flagged wherever they appear
repostWarningTravels.description: We track what happens to every posting, so we know which employers take a role down and re-list it again and again — which resets its posted date and makes an old opening look new. That warning used to appear only under the ghost-jobs heading. It now travels with the employer: if one turns up under "actually fills roles" or "states the pay", the card says so, with the number of re-postings and how many roles they were spread across. 89 employers currently qualify. It's judged on rate rather than volume, so a large employer with ordinary churn isn't flagged just for being big.

fieldsShowTheirSize.title: Every field now shows how many roles are in it
fieldsShowTheirSize.description: Browsing by field meant choosing blind — 18 labels with no way to tell which held 70,000 roles and which held 4,000. Each now carries its live count, biggest first, counted exactly the way that field's own page counts it so the two agree. 610,900 roles across all fields right now. A field too thin to be meaningful shows no number at all rather than a small one that would suggest the board is empty in your area.

listsSayWhatTheyPickedFrom.title: Each list now says what it was picked from
listsSayWhatTheyPickedFrom.description: Twelve companies under "employers that actually fill roles" reads like the whole answer, when it's the top twelve of a much larger group. Every list now states its pool: 633 employers qualify on hiring, 1,938 have five or more entry-level roles open, 818 are tracked for re-posting. The pay list says it too — 237 of the 5,011 employers with 20 or more open roles state pay on at least 80% of them, against 14% of postings board-wide. If a figure can't be computed, the sentence is left out rather than shown as zero.

exploreOneQuestion.title: Explore asks what you're looking for instead of making you scroll
exploreOneQuestion.description: The Explore page stacked every list one after another — roughly forty screens on a phone, with some of the most useful parts at the bottom where almost nobody reached them. It now opens with the question instead: check an employer, who actually hires, who states the pay, early career, ghost jobs, hiring at scale, or browse by field. You pick one and get that answer. Your choice is kept in the address bar, so a link opens on the same answer you were reading.

checkAnyEmployer.title: Look up any employer on the board, not just the ones on a list
checkAnyEmployer.description: Our lists surface about 85 companies out of more than 24,000. The tracking behind them — who fills roles, who re-lists them, who states pay — is kept for all of them, and was only visible if a company happened to top a list. You can now type any employer's name and go straight to what we've measured about them. Companies that use several hiring systems appear once instead of four times.

hiringRanksByChance.title: "Actually fills roles" now ranks by your odds, not by company size
hiringRanksByChance.description: This list was ordered by the raw number of roles an employer filled, which mostly measures how big they are: a company filling 40 of its 60 open roles could not outrank one filling 400 of 12,000, though it is far likelier to hire you. It now ranks fills against roles currently open. Small boards can't win it either — an employer needs at least 100 roles open to place, because a tiny number of openings makes the ratio meaningless. Each card also says how long its filled roles typically stayed up, and hides that line when we haven't watched the employer long enough to say.

payListWinnable.title: The pay-transparency list is winnable by employers you've heard of
payListWinnable.description: "Transparent about pay" ranked by percentage, so with only twelve places every one went to a small board sitting at exactly 100% — a company stating pay on 95% of 4,000 roles could never appear. It now ranks by how many roles actually state pay, which makes the list both honest and recognizable. The 80% threshold to qualify is unchanged.

employerNamesReal.title: Company cards show real names, and duplicates are merged
employerNamesReal.description: Some employer cards showed the internal slug from a hiring system rather than the company's name — "aloyoga" instead of ALO — and a few companies appeared as several separate entries because each of their hiring systems spelled the name differently. 38 names are corrected and the duplicates are merged. While fixing it we found the correction pass had been stopping partway through and recording itself as finished, so it now refuses to claim success unless it actually completed.

whereTheJobsComeFrom.title: See exactly where our jobs come from
whereTheJobsComeFrom.description: The front page now names all 15 applicant tracking systems we read — Workday, Greenhouse, BambooHR and the rest — each with a live count of the roles open on it right now. Every job on the board is pulled straight from one of them, never scraped from a search engine. The counts are measured rather than claimed: they move through the day and say when they were last checked.

moreRolesShowTheirDate.title: Far more roles now show when they were actually posted
moreRolesShowTheirDate.description: Two hiring systems don't publish a posting date in their job feed, so we fetch it from each posting itself. That catch-up used to run once a week, which meant a large batch of new employers could sit undated for days. It now starts as soon as a lot of undated roles arrive: BambooHR went from 23% to 38% dated and Rippling from 19% to 57%, and it keeps climbing. Knowing the real date also let us remove about 27,000 postings that turned out to be older than 30 days — our own limit — so what's left is genuinely current.

ghostIndexStatsLive.title: The Ghost Job Index numbers are current again
ghostIndexStatsLive.description: The statistics on our Ghost Job Index page had quietly stopped updating and were five days old — the page kept showing them with nothing looking wrong. They are now computed on a schedule in the background instead of when the page loads, so they stay current and carry the time they were measured. If a single figure can't be computed, the page keeps the last good one and says so rather than showing a blank.

fillSpeedSaysItsWindow.title: "Typical time to fill" now says the window it's measured in
fillSpeedSaysItsWindow.description: We publish how quickly a typical role closes after being posted. That number can only see roles that close within 30 days, because we drop postings older than that — so a role that stays open longer leaves the board instead of being counted as filled. Everywhere we quote it now says "within 30 days" outright. While fixing this we found the sentence had stopped appearing on the Ghost Job Index page altogether after an internal rename, so it's back.

moreEmployersOnTheBoard.title: 2,395 more employers on the job board
moreEmployersOnTheBoard.description: We added 2,395 company career pages in a single day, 510 of them ones our apply agent can submit to on its own. We also screen out bulk-posting agencies before they land: boards where hundreds of "openings" are the same advert repeated get held back — and a board we could not actually read is no longer treated as checked and fine.

mandateFromYourCv.title: Your agent's search now starts from your CV
mandateFromYourCv.description: When you set up a search, the roles already on your CV are offered as one-tap suggestions — each one showing the line it was read from, so you can see where it came from. We drop the seniority word (“Senior”) on purpose: employers title the same job a dozen ways, and the shorter term finds all of them. Nothing is saved until you activate it.

agentCanApplyHere.title: See which jobs the agent can apply to, before you save them
agentCanApplyHere.description: Postings our agent can fill in and submit on its own now carry an “Agent can apply” mark on the job board, in the job detail, and on your saved jobs. Most employers put bot protection on their application form, and there the agent prepares everything and you press send — now you can tell which is which before you spend time on one.

sinceYourInterview.title: What happened to the job after your interview
sinceYourInterview.description: We record the day each posting comes down from the employer's own careers feed. After an interview your tracker now says whether that exact ad was withdrawn and has stayed down, or whether the same role has gone back up. It describes the posting, not you: an ad coming down doesn't tell us who was hired.

agentSearchReach.title: Two new controls over what your agent brings you
agentSearchReach.description: You can now limit picks to jobs posted within a chosen number of days, judged on the date the employer states rather than when we happened to find it. And if you've chosen a field, you can also include postings whose field couldn't be read from the job title — about a quarter of the board, previously left out whenever a field was set.

applyAgentGuide.title: A plain guide to what the apply agent does
applyAgentGuide.description: One page covering setup, what happens overnight, the difference between review and auto mode, where the agent can and cannot submit for you, and what it will never do. It ends with the reasons a morning comes back empty — which is almost always a setting rather than a market with no jobs in it.

setupIsOneStep.title: Setting up your apply agent is now one step: upload your CV
setupIsOneStep.description: We read your name, email, phone and LinkedIn straight off the document and save it — no retyping details you just handed us. Anything an employer's form needs that a CV can't tell us is asked at the moment that form actually asks it, instead of up front. Your work authorisation, salary and start date are never guessed.

sentButUnconfirmed.title: An application we couldn't confirm no longer looks like one that needs you
sentButUnconfirmed.description: When we press send and the employer's page doesn't give us a clear confirmation, that application now reads "sent — but we couldn't confirm it", not "needs you". It used to look identical to something still waiting on you, and the natural response was to go and apply again by hand — which would have put your name in twice. We never retry it either.

agentStartsWhenYouAsk.title: Your agent starts the moment you set it up
agentStartsWhenYouAsk.description: Saving your search used to mean waiting up to an hour for the next scheduled run before anything appeared. It now begins immediately, so the first batch is ready while you're still looking at the page.

moreEmployersAutoApply.title: The agent can now apply to more employers
moreEmployersAutoApply.description: We added 148 more employer job boards on the systems our agent is able to complete end to end, chosen because they are the ones it can genuinely finish rather than the ones that merely add to the total.

agentSaysWhatItIsDoing.title: Your apply agent now tells you what it's doing
agentSaysWhatItIsDoing.description: A single line at the top of your agent section says exactly what it can and can't do right now — whether it's waiting on a setting you control, on something missing from your profile, or on us. Before, all of those looked identical: nothing happening. If the hold-up is on our side it says so plainly, and doesn't send you off to fix something that isn't broken.

applyReasonsNamed.title: Every prepared application says why it hasn't gone yet
applyReasonsNamed.description: Applications waiting in your queue now give the real reason — below the fit level you set, your daily limit reached, a question only you can answer, or already applied. And an application that has genuinely stopped now says so instead of sitting there marked ready forever, with a Try again button where retrying is safe. Where we pressed send but couldn't confirm it arrived, we say that too and deliberately don't retry, because that could apply you twice.

agentOnAtPurchase.title: Subscribing switches the agent on straight away
agentOnAtPurchase.description: Buying the apply agent now activates it the moment payment completes. Previously the entitlement was only written when you next opened your account page, so subscribing late in the evening and closing the tab meant the overnight run skipped you and no queue arrived the next morning.

tailoredCoverNotes.title: Cover notes can now be written for each job
tailoredCoverNotes.description: Until now the note attached to your applications was one paragraph, sent word for word to every employer. You can now switch on tailoring, and the agent rewrites it for each role against that job's own posting. It works only from what is already in your résumé: it cannot name an employer, a school, a skill or a figure that isn't there, and it never volunteers your visa status, salary or start date — those have their own fields, answered from what you set. Every draft is checked against your résumé and the posting before it can be used, and anything that fails the check is thrown away and your own note sent instead. It is off by default, because rewriting your words is your decision to make.

filterCountsRestored.title: Filter counts are working again
filterCountsRestored.description: The counts beside each company and category had stopped loading entirely — every visitor was getting an error after about 20 seconds. The cause was simple and entirely ours: those numbers were recounted from scratch on every single page view, three full passes over all 572,000 postings, and the board outgrew what that could finish in time. They are now worked out on a schedule and served ready-made, which takes under a second. The figures also carry the moment they were computed, so a count can tell you when it was true rather than quietly implying it is current.

applyAgentCountries.title: The apply agent won't claim you can work somewhere you haven't said
applyAgentCountries.description: It held a single yes-or-no for work authorisation and used it for every country, so someone authorised in the UK would have answered "yes" to "are you legally authorized to work in the US?" — a false statement about your immigration status, sent to an employer under your name, on the question they filter hardest on. You can now list the countries you're actually authorised to work in, and anything asking about a country you haven't listed stops and waits for you instead of guessing. Your street address and postcode can be saved too, which several application forms require and none of them will accept an approximation of.

searchFixed.title: Search works again — most searches were failing
searchFixed.description: Measured across a sample of about 40 real queries, roughly 60% were returning an error after 35 to 79 seconds. The cause was mundane: the search results and the "N results" count ran side by side, but the page still waited for the count, so a slow count held the whole response and then took it down with it — even though the results themselves were never the slow part. The count now has a time limit. Searches return in 1 to 7 seconds; if the total takes too long we show the jobs without it rather than making you wait for a number.

titleSearchFindsAll.title: Searching a job title now finds every posting with that title
titleSearchFindsAll.description: When a search matched fewer than 200 job titles we widened it to search descriptions too — and built the candidate list from the 3,000 most recent postings matching either, before ranking any of them. So a posting whose title was exactly what you typed could be discarded before ranking, simply because thousands of newer postings happened to mention those words somewhere in their text. It was then unreachable no matter how far you scrolled. Title matches now always enter the list. Re-measured live: every posting whose title matched now comes back, where before most were lost.

filterNumbersTrue.title: Filtered pages no longer report the whole board's count
filterNumbersTrue.description: Picking a field from a link like /jobs?category=Engineering filtered the jobs correctly but printed the entire board's total above them — 587,793 instead of the real number, because the capitalised spelling slipped past the check that decides whether to count at all. A second, separate version of the same slip made a work-mode filter combined with a field report 3,940 where the real figure was about 600. Both are fixed. Filter values we can't honour — a three-letter country code, an experience level that doesn't exist — are now named back to you instead of being quietly dropped while we answer the unfiltered question.

remoteAndCountryFilters.title: The Remote filter was hiding remote jobs, and the country picker never appeared
remoteAndCountryFilters.description: Two columns record whether a role is remote, and a background job that improves work-mode data updated one and not the other. They drifted apart, and the Remote filter quietly served the smaller set — thousands of genuinely remote postings it should have matched. Separately, the country control was only drawn once its list of countries loaded, and that lookup was timing out on every single attempt, so the picker never rendered at all and no country was selectable. Both fixed: the columns move together, and the control now appears whether or not the counts beside it do.

noPostingsLostPaging.title: Loading more jobs no longer skips or repeats any of them
noPostingsLostPaging.description: We had just started breaking up runs where one employer held several cards in a row, to make the first page read less repetitively. It was applied a step too early — before the page was cut — so postings could shuffle across the boundary between one page and the next: a few appeared twice, and a few were skipped and never shown again. Nobody's search should quietly lose a job. The reordering now happens only within the page you're looking at, so every posting appears exactly once. Sorting by pay is also left strictly in pay order, which it briefly wasn't.

recheckClaimCorrected.title: We were overstating how often we re-check the biggest job boards
recheckClaimCorrected.description: Our sources note said the largest boards are re-checked about every 10 to 15 minutes. Measured on 29 July across the 23,136 boards carrying a verification stamp, the median gap is about two hours and 95% are re-checked within about four hours. The claim was probably true when it was written, at a fraction of today's size, and quietly went stale as the catalogue grew past 28,000 boards. We've removed the fixed figure rather than replacing it with a new one that will age the same way — the live median and 95th percentile are published on the Ghost Job Index, where they move with the catalogue on their own.

applyNeverDeletes.title: Clicking Apply can no longer make a live job disappear
applyNeverDeletes.description: When you clicked Apply we re-checked the posting at the company's own system, and if that single check came back empty we deleted the listing. On Workday that check was wrong about 14% of the time, because Workday's search index doesn't contain every job its own pages still serve — so real, open roles were being removed by the act of applying to them. One check can no longer delete anything: a posting that looks gone is flagged, and only removed if it is still gone after a full re-read of the employer's feed.

closedJobsFullyGone.title: Roles an employer has already pulled are gone from every route
closedJobsFullyGone.description: When a company's feed stops listing a role we stop showing it — but two routes still slipped through: opening a posting by its direct link, and the sitemap we hand to search engines. A role the employer had already withdrawn could still be found through Google and still looked live, apply button and all. Both now follow the same rule as the rest of the board.

straighterBoardNumbers.title: Straighter numbers on the board and the transparency page
straighterBoardNumbers.description: Several published figures said a little more than the data supported. The board showed “updated 931 min ago” from an internal timestamp while the measured figure was under two hours — there is now one number, the measured one. Counts described as “companies” now read “company feeds”, because an employer with several hiring-system boards was being counted more than once. The transparency page names all fifteen hiring systems behind its figures instead of twelve, and its 30-day rule now says plainly that it applies to postings whose company states a date. Jobs stamped slightly ahead of our clock also no longer sit at the top of the board showing no age at all.

feedbackActuallySaved.title: Your feedback on a scan is now actually recorded
feedbackActuallySaved.description: The thumbs up/down on a scan report said “Thanks for the feedback!” every time — including when nothing was saved, which was every time, because the place it wrote to did not exist. It records properly now, and on the rare occasion it cannot, it says so instead of thanking you for nothing.

boardInYourLanguage.title: The job board now fully speaks your language
boardInYourLanguage.description: 130 pieces of the board's interface — closure notices, salary context, alert confirmations, interview-prep buttons, error messages and more — were still showing in English for Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Dutch, Hindi, Filipino and British English users. All of them are now properly translated, so the whole board reads naturally in the language you chose.

fieldFillSpeed.title: New: how fast roles in your field actually fill
fieldFillSpeed.description: Field pages now show a measured fill-speed line — for example, engineering roles typically stay open about 15 days, with 75% closing within 22. It's computed from thousands of real posting closures we tracked over the last 90 days, never an estimate, and it only appears for fields with at least 300 tracked closings. Use it to judge how quickly you need to apply.

fasterHonestBoard.title: Jobs above the fold, clearer numbers, better accessibility
fasterHonestBoard.description: The first job posting now appears higher on every screen — filter chips fit on one scrollable row instead of stacking. Job titles are real buttons screen readers can use, the close button is easier to tap, duplicate words in vendor-mangled titles are cleaned up, and salary medians now say exactly how hourly rates were annualized. Company headcounts also carry their source label everywhere they appear.

countryDetectionFix.title: Fixed: some resumes were matched to the wrong country's market
countryDetectionFix.description: A detection bug could read cloud terms like “EC2” as a London postcode and miss US phone numbers written without +1, so some US resumes received market advice for the United Kingdom — presented confidently. That is exactly the failure this product exists to avoid, and it is fixed: 22 regression tests now pin the failure cases, ambiguous resumes defer to your actual location instead of a coin flip, and every report now records how your market was chosen — your selection, resume evidence, or location — so a guess can never again dress up as certainty.

semanticSearch.title: Search now understands meaning, not just words
semanticSearch.description: When a search finds no title matches, the board now looks for roles that mean the same thing — “infosec analyst” can surface security engineer openings even when no posting contains your exact words. The page says clearly when results are meaning-based matches, and your filters are never silently dropped to make it happen.

morningEmails.title: The emails you signed up for now actually send
morningEmails.description: Two email loops were built, opted into, and never wired to a schedule — so nobody ever received them. Fixed: Apply Agent's overnight shortlist now arrives each morning with the same reasons the queue shows, and market-pulse subscribers finally get their monthly digest. Both are opt-in — at most one morning email a day and one pulse a month — with one-click unsubscribe.

fullJobDescriptions.title: Job descriptions now load on far more roles
fullJobDescriptions.description: Some employers publish their job text through a separate feed we were not reading, so a large share of postings opened with nothing to read and fit scoring had no text to work with. We now pull that text for Workday, BambooHR, SmartRecruiters, Breezy and Oracle boards, and Workable and Pinpoint descriptions now arrive with the listing itself. Anything you open is saved, so it loads instantly next time. Where an employer genuinely publishes no description, we still show nothing rather than a guess.

accountHq.title: Your account is now mission control
accountHq.description: The account got a real overhaul: a sticky section nav (Overview, Pipeline, Searches, Résumé) so nothing is buried; a 'What to fix next' report showing the skills most often missing from your résumé across your target roles — with counts, and one click to work them in via the builder; upcoming interviews stitched into one glance; a setup checklist that walks new accounts into the full search loop; a clear path into the Morning Queue; and every weekly email toggle in a single Emails & alerts panel.

boardContinuity.title: Smoother board: applied badges, a better first visit, mobile polish
boardContinuity.description: Postings you've already applied to now wear a quiet check on cards and in compare — you'll never re-read a job you already acted on without knowing it. Your application tracker also shows each employer's pattern (genuinely fills roles, or re-lists often) right where you're waiting to hear back. First-time visitors get three one-tap starting points — posted today, companies that fill roles, stated pay only. On phones, descriptions lead and sections start folded; and employer facts now load with a placeholder instead of popping in late.

decisionPanel.title: Company facts where you decide — plus tidier job descriptions
decisionPanel.description: The job detail panel now shows who you'd actually be joining: verified headcount, public-company revenue and profitability, and (for H-1B filers) declared wages — the same sourced facts from company pages, now beside every posting. Long descriptions fold into collapsible sections when the posting itself has clear headings, with your keyword highlights preserved. Comparing jobs now includes work mode, company size and financials; the board says how it's ordered; and signed-in users get their saved searches as one-tap chips.

secFilings.title: Know the company: SEC filings on hiring pages
secFilings.description: Company pages for 178 US-listed employers now show what kind of company you'd actually be joining — revenue over the last three fiscal years with a mini trend, whether the company is profitable, and its ticker — all pulled from the company's own SEC filings (10-K/20-F), with a link to the source. As filed, never estimated.

payTransparency.title: Definitive work-mode tags, full salary ranges, and the Pay Transparency Index
payTransparency.description: Remote, hybrid, and on-site are now three definitive tags, taken from the employer's own ATS field or explicit posting text — and shown only when the employer actually says (no tag is honest, a guessed tag is not). Salary now stores and shows the full stated range with its original period, hourly and monthly figures get an annualized line, and filters match only stated pay. And it's all public: the new Pay Transparency Index ranks fields, hiring systems, and large employers by how much of their postings state pay, and Explore gained a Transparent-about-pay collection no company can buy its way into.

fairDataPromise.title: A fair-data promise, verified employers, and 7 free Agent mornings
fairDataPromise.description: Three things shipped together. First, policy in writing: no company can pay to change what our data says — fill rates, churn flags, and badges are computed from observed postings and are not for sale (see the Trust page). Second, employers can now claim their company page by verifying a work email at their own domain, earning a Verified employer badge — identity only, never editing rights. Third, the Apply Agent now starts with 7 free mornings, so you can wake up to a real shortlist before paying anything.

companyIntel.title: Company pages that actually tell you about the company
companyIntel.description: Every company page now leads with sourced facts: verified headcount with its basis, this week's net-new roles, the company's own stated-salary median, and its top hiring fields. Below the postings, a 'similar companies' section shows who else is hiring in the same field. The Explore scale segments got hundreds more verified headcounts (Bosch, H&M, GM, Tyson and more) and every band now expands to its full company list.

board450k.title: 450,000+ verified openings — Pinpoint joins as the 13th hiring system
board450k.description: Another growth wave: 450,000+ live openings from 20,000+ companies, all straight from each company's own hiring system. New this round: Pinpoint as the 13th system, Greenhouse's separate EU platform (hundreds of European employers), and thousands more boards found in deeper archive sweeps. We also tightened the door: this is a corporate board, and a handful of government job boards that had slipped in were removed — public-sector listings don't belong here and won't get in again.

smartSearch.title: Search that understands what you're looking for
smartSearch.description: Search got a brain. Results are ranked by relevance — title matches first, company and team next — and searches now look inside full job descriptions too, so niche skills surface even when they're not in the title. The search box suggests as you type (your recent searches, companies, categories, common roles), quoted "exact phrases" work, one tap flips between relevance and newest-first, and category pills with live counts show the board's whole breadth at a glance.

boardCraft.title: A faster, friendlier board — on every device
boardCraft.description: A pile of quality-of-life upgrades: press ⌘K anywhere for quick actions, ? shows all keyboard shortcuts, and / jumps to search. The company filter is a type-ahead now, a compact view fits three times more postings per screen, "Jump back in" brings back your recently viewed roles, and every posting has a share link. Each posting also shows when it was last re-verified against the company's feed, pay displays consistently (the company's exact wording one hover away), and the mobile layout got a full pass.

board300k.title: 300,000+ verified openings — Workday joins as the 12th hiring system
board300k.description: The board tripled in a week: 300,000+ live openings from 16,000+ companies, every one pulled straight from the company's own hiring system. New this round: Workday — the system used by many of the world's largest employers — plus thousands of newly discovered company boards across all twelve systems.

freshFirst.title: Fresh jobs first: honest date filters and faster discovery of new postings
freshFirst.description: The Today and This-week filters now count only dates the company itself stated — never our discovery time. Boards that post new roles frequently are now re-checked more often, so new openings appear here sooner. Workday postings carry the company's stated posting age from the moment they arrive.

accurateDates.title: Posting ages you can trust — plus a country filter
accurateDates.description: Every posting-age stat now uses only company-stated dates, and each card says where its date came from. Salary sorting is currency-aware, so a peso figure can't outrank a dollar one. And you can now filter the board by country — 60+ countries, matched only when the posting itself says so.

matchingResume.title: Pin the exact resume the whole platform matches against
matchingResume.description: Your account now holds an explicit matching resume: pin any scan that saved its document, or paste the exact resume you're sending out, and the job board's fit ranking, your match-alert emails, and the apply agent's drafts all ground against that document. If you don't pin anything, nothing changes — everything keeps using your latest scan, as it always has.

ghostJobIndex.title: The Ghost Job Index: we audit our own board and publish the number
ghostJobIndex.description: A new public page shows the live, honest numbers behind the board: how many verified roles are open right now, the median age of a posting, how fast roles actually get filled, and which companies are hiring most actively. Behind it, the board now audits itself every day — sampling about a hundred random listings and re-checking each one against the company's own system — and publishes the confirmed-live percentage for everyone to see. The guarantees that were always true are now stated up front too: nothing older than 30 days stays listed, and every posting is re-checked live the moment you click Apply.

hiringHealth.title: Hiring Health: see which companies actually fill roles
hiringHealth.description: The board now follows the full lifecycle of every posting — when it opens and when the company takes it down — and turns that into a signal no aggregator can offer. Company pages show how many roles a company filled or closed in the last 90 days and how quickly, an "Actively hiring" badge marks companies with a proven recent pattern, and a board filter lets you browse only those. Built honestly: where there isn't enough data yet, the panel says it's still gathering rather than guessing.

salaryAndDedupe.title: Salary on more postings, and the same role no longer floods the list
salaryAndDedupe.description: Many companies state the pay range in the posting text even when their hiring system has no salary field — the board now reads it from the posting's own words, never an estimate, so salary appears on more and more cards over the coming weeks. When a company posts the same role across many locations, you now see one card with a "same role in N more locations" expander instead of a wall of near-identical listings — every location stays applyable. And company pages now answer the question people actually search — "is this company hiring?" — with a live, verified count.

applyAgent.title: The apply agent: real application questions, answered from your resume — never invented
applyAgent.description: Greenhouse postings now carry a "Prep answers" button. The agent pulls the application's real questions from the company's own system, drafts answers grounded strictly in your resume, and flags anything it can't support instead of inventing it — identity, salary, and demographic questions are always left to you. The same panel tailors your resume for the role, drafts a cover letter, preps likely interview questions, warns you if you already applied, and states the honesty guarantee up front. You review everything and submit on the company's own site — it never applies for you.

explainableFit.title: Fit you can read — what you have, what to add, and alerts only for strong matches
explainableFit.description: Fit-ranked cards now show both sides of the score: "You already have:" alongside "Add to compete:", so the ranking explains itself instead of being a bare number. Saved-search emails gain a fit bar — choose "strong fit only" and we email you only about new roles that clear it, scored against your resume, staying silent otherwise. And once you have enough tracked applications, your account shows your interview rate by the fit you applied with — so you can see where your applications actually convert.

boardScaleUp.title: Company pool more than doubles: 8,600+ verified employers on the board
boardScaleUp.description: A database upgrade removed the board's old capacity ceiling, so every remaining clean employer from our census of the major hiring platforms came aboard — the pool grew from about 3,900 to more than 8,600 companies, each one live-verified against its platform's official public API and named from the platform's own records. Live postings are climbing as the new boards stream in, under the same rules as always: every job comes straight from the company's own board, aggregators and staffing mills are excluded, and nothing older than 30 days stays listed. The board got cleaner and faster in the same pass — a handful of companies that appeared twice under differently-cased board names were deduplicated, misfiled roles (optometrists, art directors, preschool teachers) moved out of “Other” into their proper fields, and the jobs page payload slimmed by half so filtering feels snappier.

comeBackSignals.title: Your account now tells you when it's worth coming back
comeBackSignals.description: Three quieter upgrades that turn the board into a loop instead of a one-time visit. The weekly email digest for saved searches now actually sends — it had an opt-in toggle but nothing scheduled behind it, so opted-in searches silently got nothing; now they get a weekly-ish email when new postings match, with a working one-click unsubscribe. Your account's saved-search card leads with the total that matters: how many new jobs match your saved searches since your last visit, one click from the search with the most. And when a posting you applied to gets taken down, the tracker no longer leaves you at a dead end — it pulls live openings for the same role straight off the board so you keep momentum.

fitFirstBoard.title: The board now opens ranked to your resume
fitFirstBoard.description: Scan your resume once and the board opens already sorted by fit — no extra click. Each listing shows a plain-language match tier (Strong match, Possible match, or Stretch) rather than a raw percentage, with the exact keyword coverage on hover and the specific terms to add to compete. Every card is marked as pulled straight from that company's official careers feed — never an aggregator or a scraped copy — and re-checked live the moment you click Apply. In your account, the application co-pilot now preps your strongest-matched saved jobs first, so if you reach the daily limit the best ones are already done.

fieldPages.title: Browse the job board by field: 17 dedicated pages with live counts
fieldPages.description: Every field on the board — Engineering & IT, Healthcare & Clinical, Finance & Accounting, Hospitality & Retail, and 13 more — now has its own page at /jobs/field with that field's live openings and the filter already set. Each page shows the field's real posting count, measured from the live corpus when the site was last built (Engineering & IT: 21,610 at this writing). Our 59 industry keyword guides link straight to their matching field, in English and Spanish. Same rules as everywhere on the board: official company feeds only, and applying happens on the company's own site.

boardSelfTuning.title: The board now tunes and monitors itself
boardSelfTuning.description: Three quieter upgrades behind the 90,000-posting board. The fast lane re-ranks itself: after every refresh pass, the boards with the most live openings automatically get the fastest re-check cadence, so a company on a hiring spree speeds up without anyone touching a setting. Postings that arrive without a published date (some feeds never include one) now use their first-seen time for sorting and freshness filters, so they can't sink to the bottom unseen — displayed dates remain only what the company actually published. And the refresh pipeline watches itself: if it ever stalls, we're alerted within the hour, before the board goes stale enough for anyone to notice. Categorization got sharper too — corporate IT, service desk, research, investor relations, district management, and French retail roles arriving now file into their proper fields instead of Other.

board90k.title: Job board doubles: ~90,000 live postings across nearly 900 companies
board90k.description: The board grew from roughly 40,000 to roughly 90,000 live postings. New this round: major employers like AECOM, Domino's, SGS, Veolia, Carvana, Turner & Townsend, Eurofins, Sopra Steria, Greene King, BAYADA Home Health Care, CROSSMARK, EōS Fitness and BoxLunch — heavy on healthcare, engineering, food service, retail, hospitality and lab work, not just tech. Every company joined the same way: found in a census of the major hiring platforms, then verified against the platform's official public API and named from the platform's own records. We also found aggregators and reposted-listing feeds in that census and excluded them — every posting here belongs to the company that published it. The refresh got smarter with the size: the largest boards are re-checked most often and the whole catalog is re-verified within a few hours, so postings a company takes down keep disappearing on the next pass.

suiteV2.title: Simpler pricing, a real guarantee, and apply-for-this-job help
suiteV2.description: Three changes to how the paid tools work. Pricing now leads with three clear choices instead of a wall of thirteen — the full catalog is still there, one click away. Every paid tool now carries a make-it-right promise: not happy with the output? We'll regenerate it free. And after you check your resume against a real posting, the report can now prepare that exact application — resume tailored to the job, matching cover letter, honest gap list — with a free preview from your own resume before you pay.

roleTargeting.title: Your report now tells you what to apply for
roleTargeting.description: Every free scan now ends with a game plan, not just a grade. A new card lists the roles your resume actually screens for — drawn from the same detection your score used, with search links pre-aimed at your target market — plus the roles within reach through your secondary strength, with an honest note on what the gap really is. And if you scanned without a job posting, the report now leads with the single highest-leverage next step: paste a real opening and rescan against its exact requirements, free.

countryCvPages.title: CV rules for 56 countries — free, in 6 languages
countryCvPages.description: New: a per-country guide to what a CV actually looks like in 56 markets — photo norms (with the real stats and laws), expected length, personal-data conventions, and the local document's name. Built from the same engine the scanner uses when your resume targets that market, with pages in English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, and Dutch. Start at /cv-standards.

sharperGeo.title: The scan now follows where you're going, not just where you've been
sharperGeo.description: Write "relocating to London" or "seeking roles in Germany" and the scan now benchmarks against your destination market — previously it judged you by your current location. It also reads real addresses (a US state + ZIP, a Canadian postal code, a German street address) as stronger evidence than a city name in a bullet, detects ~34 more countries, and a specialist second field (like a nurse who builds machine-learning models) now shows up instead of being drowned out by the primary profession.

resumeLanguageReports.title: Your report now speaks your résumé's language
resumeLanguageReports.description: Scan a résumé written in French, Spanish, German, Portuguese, Dutch, Italian, Hindi or Tagalog and the entire report — tips, red flags, rewrites, keyword suggestions — comes back in that language. This worked only sometimes before; now the language is detected reliably before the analysis starts, so it's no longer a coin flip. Bonus: the language your résumé is written in also helps pin down which job market you're in, so location-specific advice lands on the right country.

sharperDetection.title: Sharper location & industry detection
sharperDetection.description: Your report now follows the market you're actually in — even if your résumé name-drops other cities. We weigh real signals (where you're authorized to work, your education system, your phone number) over a passing city mention, so a US candidate who "led the London launch" is still benchmarked against the US market. Cross-functional résumés also surface a genuine second field — a Sales Director who was also a Marketing Manager gets both covered.

previewBeforePay.title: See a real sample of any paid tool before you buy
previewBeforePay.description: No more buying blind. Every paid tool now generates a real slice of what you'd get — built from your own résumé — before you pay. Interview Coach shows one real question, the rewrite tools show a true before-and-after of one of your own bullets, and Freelance Boost turns one of your projects into a recruiter-grade line. Same integrity as the paid version: if your résumé doesn't support a metric, we won't invent one.

sharperPaidProducts.title: Sharper Freelance Boost & Interview Coach
sharperPaidProducts.description: Both now generate with our most capable model — noticeably stronger, more specific output on the resume sections and interview prep you pay for. Same grounded, nothing-invented approach; better engine behind it.

smarterIndustryConfirm.title: The scan now asks when your field is a genuine toss-up
smarterIndustryConfirm.description: If your resume straddles two fields — say marketing and business development, or clinical work and data science — the scan now flags the industry for you to confirm before committing, instead of quietly picking one and risking the wrong call.

liveBenchmarks.title: See how real resumes score: live ATS benchmarks
liveBenchmarks.description: The benchmarks page now shows live ATS-score distributions from our real scan corpus — overall median and quartiles, per-industry benchmarks, and experience-level medians, each labeled with its sample size. The homepage scan counter now reflects the real all-time total too.

reportCardsFix.title: Fixed: parts of your report weren't showing
reportCardsFix.description: A display bug quietly hid several report sections on some scans — country-specific resume standards, the ATS parsing breakdown, quick wins, and the ATS-vs-recruiter score among them. They're all back. We also added an automated safeguard so a whole section can't silently go missing again.

targetMarketScan.title: Applying abroad? Your report now follows the job, not your home country
targetMarketScan.description: Targeting a role in another country? Choose where you're applying and the scan checks your resume against that market's norms — photo and personal-data expectations, references, and more — instead of assuming your current location. We also expanded automatic country detection so more resumes get the right local rules on their own.

groundedAnalysis.title: Fewer false 'you're missing this' flags
groundedAnalysis.description: Before analyzing, the scanner now maps your resume's real structure — sections, dated roles, contact details — so it's much less likely to tell you something is missing when it's actually there. And when a PDF doesn't extract cleanly, we now warn you the results may be unreliable instead of scoring scrambled text.

guidesTab.title: All our guides in one place
guidesTab.description: A new Guides tab collects every how-to we've written — why resumes get rejected, choosing the right keywords, career-change and freelance resumes, and more. 'How It Works' now lives on the Trust page next to our methodology.

honestClaims.title: Our claims now match our own research
honestClaims.description: We reviewed the whole site and rewrote anything that overstated how resume screening works. No invented statistics and no scare tactics — what we tell you lines up with what our own analysis of ATS behavior actually shows.

countryStandards.title: Your report now knows local rules: 52-country resume standards
countryStandards.description: Scanning from Germany, Japan, or the Gulf? Your report now includes your market's norms — photo rules (the highest-stakes difference: a photo is expected in Tokyo and gets you discarded in Toronto), personal-data expectations, and market-specific checks like Poland's RODO clause, Italy's privacy consent, and Gulf visa-status lines. Verified July 2026; softer markets are labeled as directional.

fractionalMode.title: Fractional leaders: concurrent roles are a portfolio, not job-hopping
fractionalMode.description: The scanner now recognizes fractional and interim leadership — overlapping senior engagements no longer get misread as instability. And Freelance Boost gained a fractional mode: an umbrella portfolio entry with per-engagement scope (P&L, headcount, stage), built only from figures you provide. Plus a new guide on structuring fractional roles.

freelanceUpgrades.title: Freelance Boost: see the transformation before you pay
freelanceUpgrades.description: The intake page now shows a labeled before/after example of what the translation actually produces. Paste an Upwork-style profile into the free scanner and it says the honest thing — 'this is a profile, not a resume' — and routes you to the right tool. And results now insert directly into the builder as real experience entries, ready for typeset export.

honestMetricsFix.title: Fixed: some report tiles showed defaults instead of your data
honestMetricsFix.description: An internal audit found that when the analysis omitted certain metrics, the report quietly filled them with identical defaults for everyone — including a per-ATS compatibility list that was never real. All of it is gone: those metrics are now required from the analysis, word/page counts derive from your actual document, and anything we can't measure is hidden instead of invented. We publish this because trust is the product.

coachButtonFix.title: Fixed: the $5 Interview Coach button opened the $25 checkout
coachButtonFix.description: The 'Interview Coach — $5' offer at the end of the report was routing into the $25 Full Analysis checkout. It now buys exactly what it says. If this happened to you, contact us for a refund — no questions.

shareCards.title: Share your before/after — and your roast
shareCards.description: One tap now opens your phone's share sheet with a clean image attached. Rescanned after fixing? The card becomes your improvement: '58 → 74, same rubric both times.' And the Resume Roast finally gets the shareable image it deserves — burn quote, spice level, no resume content ever on any card.

fallbackParity.title: The backup scanner is now as good as the main one
fallbackParity.description: Our emergency fallback scanner had drifted: older detection tables and a slower model (about 32s vs 20s). It now runs the exact same detection data as the primary — Spanish included — and the faster model order. You'd only ever meet it during an outage; now it would be a much better meeting.

paidDeliverablesAudit.title: We audited our own paid products like a ruthless editor
paidDeliverablesAudit.description: We generated and reviewed every flagship deliverable. Findings, fixed the same day: cover letters could contain [bracketed placeholders] — now banned; letters must arrive send-ready. The premium rewrite once invented a LinkedIn URL — now a code-level contact-integrity guard strips any contact detail not present in your original, on top of stricter prompts. Interview-coach sample answers now stay grounded in your real resume.

typesetDelivery.title: Premium rewrites now become real documents
typesetDelivery.description: The Premium Package's rewritten resume can now open directly in the free builder — one click and it's a professionally typeset PDF or Word document, ready to send, instead of text on a webpage.

rescanRitual.title: See your before/after — fix, export, rescan
rescanRitual.description: Export from the builder and you're offered a one-click rescan of that exact version. The new report opens with the delta: '58 → 74, red flags 5 → 2 — same rubric both times.' Improvement you can measure, not just feel.

applicationFit.title: Check any application's fit against the version you actually sent
applicationFit.description: In your application tracker, paste the job posting and see which recognized keywords the resume version you sent covers — and which are missing. Deterministic and reproducible: the dictionary is our scanner's own detection tables, no AI involved.

fixPlanDrip.title: Your fix plan as a 7-day sequence — strictly opt-in
fixPlanDrip.description: A new unchecked-by-default option when you email yourself a report: your top fixes on day 2, the rest on day 4, a rescan reminder on day 6. Three emails total, built from your actual fix roadmap, with one-click unsubscribe that cancels the remaining ones too.

personalOutcomeAnalytics.title: Your own interview rate, by score band
personalOutcomeAnalytics.description: Once you've tracked 5+ applications with statuses, your account shows the interview rate of your own applications grouped by resume score — your personal evidence of what works, with honest small-sample framing.

emailSuppressionFix.title: Fixed: unsubscribing now cancels queued emails too
emailSuppressionFix.description: Our email queue wasn't checking the suppression list before sending — so bounces, complaints, and unsubscribes weren't fully enforced for queued mail. Now every non-security email checks the list at send time. Found while building the fix-plan sequence; fixed for everything.

outcomeTracking.title: Tell us how it went — outcome tracking begins
outcomeTracking.description: After every scan you can now report — anonymously — whether that resume got interviews, right in the report or from your emailed summary. As answers accumulate we'll publish measured score-to-interview data instead of the folklore this industry usually sells.

savedVersions.title: Save resume versions — and see which one lands interviews
savedVersions.description: Signed-in users can save the exact document behind any scan (only when you ask — the free scan still never stores your resume). Tag each application with the version you sent, and your account shows which version actually gets interviews.

builderFixHandoff.title: One click from diagnosis to a fixed resume
builderFixHandoff.description: The report now ends with 'Open in builder with fixes applied': your resume lands in the free builder with the report's bullet rewrites already in place and missing keywords suggested alongside. We never auto-insert keywords — only you can honestly claim a skill.

transitionProTier.title: Transition Pro: the complete career-change kit
transitionProTier.description: The $59 tier is now genuinely more than the $29 one: everything in Freelance Boost, plus a complete transition cover letter and a LinkedIn About section — built from your real projects under the same no-invention rules.

spanishCoverLetters.title: Spanish job posting? Spanish cover letter
spanishCoverLetters.description: Cover letters now detect the language of the job posting and write natural, professional Spanish when the posting is Spanish. Scan reports have always answered in your resume's language.

scanLimitDoubleCountFix.title: Fixed: scans were counting twice against your daily limit
scanLimitDoubleCountFix.description: A background pre-scan was quietly consuming a second daily slot — and running a full analysis whose results were never shown. If you ever hit the scan limit faster than expected, this was why. Your free scans per day are now exactly what we advertise.

guidesLaunch.title: Six guides that tell you the truth about ATS
guidesLaunch.description: New guides grounded in the checks our scanner actually runs — including one debunking the '75% of resumes are rejected by bots' myth our industry loves. Each opens with a short, direct answer. No recycled folklore.

outageSentinel.title: Outages now get caught in minutes, not hours
outageSentinel.description: A monitoring sentinel runs a real scan through the live system every 10 minutes and alerts us the moment anything breaks, with an independent backstop outside our own infrastructure. After the July 4th outage we promised structural fixes — this is them.

homepageLiveStats.title: Real scan statistics, right on the front page
homepageLiveStats.description: The homepage now shows how real resumes actually score: live median, middle-half range, share scoring 80 or higher, and the full score distribution — drawn from the same public data as our benchmark study. If the live data can't be loaded, the section shows nothing rather than invented numbers.

scoreBenchmarksStudy.title: What's a good ATS score? Now answered with live data
scoreBenchmarksStudy.description: A new research page publishes real score benchmarks computed live from scans on this site: overall median and quartiles, per-industry distributions, and experience-level medians over a rolling 180-day window. Aggregates only — at least 25 scans per bucket, and no individual resume data is ever exposed.

syntheticScanExclusion.title: Our own test scans no longer count in the stats
syntheticScanExclusion.description: The monitoring probes and load tests we run to keep the scanner healthy are now tagged as test traffic and excluded from every published statistic, and past test scans were retroactively removed. The benchmarks you see reflect real resumes only.

scanOutageFix.title: Fixed: a brief scan outage — and the gap that allowed it
scanOutageFix.description: For a short window today, free scans returned an error due to a defect in a new release. It's fixed, and we've added a deeper automated check to our release process that catches this entire class of bug before it ships — plus, in the process, we found and fixed a long-standing flaw in our garbled-text detector. Transparency is the product; that includes our mistakes.

freelanceBoostLaunch.title: New product: Freelance Boost
freelanceBoostLaunch.description: Turn freelance projects, gig work, and side hustles into recruiter-grade resume experience. A guided intake (no resume needed), your projects translated into the target field's language, the right structure chosen for your situation, honest gap handling, and keyword coverage against your target posting. Import your Upwork/Fiverr profile text or LinkedIn PDF to pre-fill the form. $29, one-time.

roastUpgrade.title: Resume Roast actually roasts now
roastUpgrade.description: The Roast was rebuilt around real roast-comedy craft: every burn quotes your actual resume verbatim and dismantles exactly those words — and any roast built on an invented quote is thrown out before you see it. The serious recruiter insight still follows every hit.

reliabilityAtScale.title: Built for crowds
reliabilityAtScale.description: Under heavy traffic the platform now degrades gracefully instead of slowing down: past capacity, scans instantly receive the full deterministic report with a free AI-enhanced rescan minutes later — no timeouts, no multi-minute waits, ever.

diagnosticReport.title: Your free scan is now a diagnostic report
diagnosticReport.description: The report has been redesigned around a diagnostic structure: a specimen header with a unique report ID (rescanning the same document reproduces it), a findings summary — critical, warnings, passed — before any detail, findings that run uninterrupted, and all offers consolidated in one clearly-marked Next Steps section at the end.

onetSourcing.title: Keyword expectations, sourced from the U.S. Department of Labor
onetSourcing.description: Resume-only scans now draw expected skills and technologies from O*NET — the Department of Labor's occupational database — with the source and occupation code shown in your report. A pasted job posting still overrides everything: the employer's actual ask beats any database.

honestScoring.title: Honest scoring: bands, provenance, and real extraction
honestScoring.description: Your score now shows its modeling band instead of false single-point precision. Every report states where its expectations came from — the exact job posting, O*NET, or our model. And when you upload a file, the parse preview is labeled for what it is: the actual text extracted from your document, the same operation an ATS performs.

reportEverywhere.title: The same report on screen, in PDF, and in your inbox
reportEverywhere.description: The downloadable PDF and the emailed report now carry the full diagnostic structure — same report ID, findings summary, score band, and source attributions as the on-screen version. One consistent document you can save, print, or forward.

fasterScans.title: Faster scans — and instant rescans
fasterScans.description: Two engine upgrades: repeat scans of the same resume now return in about a second, and the analysis pipeline was rebuilt to run its AI passes in parallel on a faster model, cutting fresh-scan wait times substantially.

freelanceGuidance.title: Freelancers get their own playbook
freelanceGuidance.description: The scan now detects freelance and project-based careers (or tell it with the new Freelancing chip) and shows how to position client work as one coherent track — your actual projects turned into experience bullets, plus advice for moving into employment.

spanishDetection.title: Full Spanish resume support
spanishDetection.description: Industry detection now reads fully Spanish resumes natively — around 200 Spanish job titles and industry terms across 15 fields (enfermería, contabilidad, ventas, obra civil and more), not just translated headings.

industryScreenerChecks.title: What screeners in YOUR field look for
industryScreenerChecks.description: New field-specific checks: portfolio links for creative roles, GitHub for engineers, publications for researchers, security clearance for government work, and license visibility for healthcare, legal, trades and 8 more licensed fields — each with exactly what to fix.

realBenchmarks.title: Benchmarks from real scans
realBenchmarks.description: As each industry accumulates enough scans on our platform, your score comparison switches from estimates to the actual distribution of real resumes scanned here — and the report tells you when that's the case.

builderExports.title: Resume Builder exports, professionally typeset
builderExports.description: DOCX exports now use clean black section headings with hairline rules (no more default Word styling), dates aligned to the true right margin, and a consistent type scale. PDF exports fixed page-break orphans and bullet indentation.

proSubscription.title: Resume Booster Pro — every tool, one subscription
proSubscription.description: New $45/month all-access plan: every paid tool included (Full Analysis, Keyword Fix, Cover Letters, Interview Coach, and more), unlimited daily scans, and every new tool we launch — included automatically. Cancel anytime.

scoreSimulator.title: See your score before you fix anything
scoreSimulator.description: The report now includes an interactive simulator: check off the fixes you plan to make and watch your projected ATS score update instantly — so you know which fixes are worth your time before you touch your resume.

weakestBullets.title: Your 3 weakest bullets, graded and rewritten
weakestBullets.description: The scan now quotes your three weakest bullet points verbatim, grades each one A–F on metrics, verbs, and scope, and shows an improved rewrite built only from what's already on your resume.

atsVendorChecks.title: How Workday, Greenhouse, Lever & iCIMS read your resume
atsVendorChecks.description: Each major ATS parses resumes differently. Your report now shows a vendor-by-vendor check of how your specific formatting survives each system — and what to change if it doesn't.

careerChangeBridge.title: Career changers get a transfer map
careerChangeBridge.description: Switching fields? The report now detects transitions and shows which of your skills carry over as-is, which lines to reword for the new field, and the single biggest credibility gap to close.

scoreAuditTrail.title: Why this score? Every point accounted for
scoreAuditTrail.description: A new expandable audit shows exactly where your ATS score comes from — keyword coverage, format, quantified impact, and content signals, each with earned points that sum to your total.

shareScoreCard.title: Share your score
shareScoreCard.description: One click downloads a clean score-card image — your score, industry, and percentile, with no resume content on it — ready to share anywhere.

verifiedReportClaims.title: Every quote in your report is now verified
verifiedReportClaims.description: Before your report is shown, every claimed quote from your resume is checked against the actual text — anything that doesn't match is removed and rebuilt from verified analysis. What the report says about your resume is really in your resume.

smarterIndustryDetection.title: Sharper industry detection
smarterIndustryDetection.description: 133 new job-title variants across 45 industries, a tiebreaker for close calls, automatic career-transition detection, and a feedback loop that learns from your corrections — plus benchmarks that calibrate to your target job's industry when you paste a job description.

fasterFrontPage.title: A faster front page with instant upload
fasterFrontPage.description: The homepage now loads dramatically less code up front, and you can drop your resume directly in the hero — no scrolling, no hunting for the upload box.

tenNewIndustries.title: 10 new industries now fully supported
tenNewIndustries.description: The scanner now has dedicated keyword libraries, job-title recognition, certification tables, and scoring benchmarks for 10 more fields: cybersecurity, logistics & supply chain, real estate, insurance, nonprofit & fundraising, biotech & lab science, aviation, energy, skilled trades (electricians, plumbers, HVAC, welders and more), and customer support. If you work in one of these fields, your scan is no longer squeezed into a loosely-related category — keywords, red flags, and benchmarks are now specific to your actual profession.

specializationDetection.title: Specialization-level industry detection
specializationDetection.description: Broad industries hide very different jobs — a nurse, a medical biller, and a pharma sales rep are all "healthcare" but need completely different resumes. The scanner now detects your specialization within the industry (clinical care vs. healthcare administration vs. pharma vs. health tech; frontend vs. backend vs. DevOps; accounting vs. FP&A vs. investment banking, and more) and tailors every recommendation to it. Professional licenses like RN, CPA, PE, CISSP, or a journeyman card now anchor the classification, and when you paste a job description, the analysis is framed around the field you're applying INTO. Cross-functional resumes get an honest blend readout (e.g. "60% data / 40% marketing") instead of being forced into one box.

interviewLikelihoodFixPlan.title: Interview likelihood and a minute-by-minute fix plan
interviewLikelihoodFixPlan.description: Three new results tell you where you stand and exactly what to do next. An interview callback likelihood band combines your ATS pass rate, peer percentile, and critical red flags into one honest verdict — with the single biggest factor holding you back named explicitly. A side-by-side comparison shows how your resume stacks up against a top-quartile candidate in your field on quantified bullets, leadership signals, and keyword coverage. And a numbered fix plan sequences everything into a single work session, ordered by points gained per minute, with a running projected score after each step.

deeperScoreReporting.title: See exactly what drives your score
deeperScoreReporting.description: Your ATS score is no longer a single opaque number. A score breakdown shows the three components — keyword match, format, and quantification — as separate bars. Quick wins now carry explicit point values and are sorted by impact. You get three bullet rewrites instead of one, a severity ranking on every red flag (critical / moderate / minor), the specific issues that drove your format grade, quality ratings for each resume section, a recruiter first-pass verdict written as a 6-second scan, and one clear next best action to take.

atsPreviewComparisons.title: See your resume the way an ATS does
atsPreviewComparisons.description: A new parse preview shows the raw text an applicant tracking system actually extracts from your resume — formatting, columns, and icons stripped away — so you can spot content that gets lost before a human ever sees it. Alongside it: your percentile against other candidates in your industry, an estimated ATS pass rate, a keyword gap heat map that shows how often each missing keyword appears in real job postings (with advice on which section to add it to), a tone & voice audit that counts passive phrases and first-person pronouns, and a section length audit comparing each section against ideal word-count targets.

trulyPersonalReports.title: Every scan is now written specifically about you
trulyPersonalReports.description: Generic advice is now treated as a failure. Every red flag, weak phrase, and quick win must quote your actual resume text verbatim — not "your bullets lack metrics" but exactly which bullet, quoted back to you. Advice is calibrated to your seniority: executives are never told to "add more keywords," and entry-level candidates are never asked about P&L ownership. Career changers get transferable-skills mapping, veterans get military-to-civilian translation, returners get gap-framing language, and recent grads get project elevation advice. Your name and role now run throughout the report.

industryDetectionAccuracy8Fixes.title: 8 accuracy upgrades to industry detection
industryDetectionAccuracy8Fixes.description: We identified and fixed every known category of industry misclassification. (1) Unambiguous role titles — registered nurse, attorney, product manager, ML engineer, and 50+ others — now hard-lock the industry regardless of keyword scores, so a nurse with Python in her skills section is never classified as a data scientist. (2) Each industry now requires at least one anchor term to be present before high confidence is granted — eliminating false positives caused by long skills lists. (3) Very short resumes (under 80 words) skip keyword scoring entirely and rely only on your job titles. (4) The employer name boost is now guarded — a finance analyst at Google no longer gets a technology boost. (5) Implausible industry + seniority combinations (e.g. entry-level consulting, executive retail) are flagged and confidence is capped. (6) The skills section contribution is now hard-capped at 6 points regardless of how many skills are listed — your most recent job titles always outweigh a 60-item skills list. (7) When you paste a job description alongside your resume, the AI now classifies your industry from your resume titles, not the company you're applying to. (8) User corrections now compound logarithmically — the more times a pattern is corrected, the stronger the learning signal.

marketIntelligenceCards.title: Live market intelligence in your scan results
marketIntelligenceCards.description: Your scan now includes five new data cards below your main results. The Market Intelligence card shows the job market conditions for your industry in your country — hot skills right now, rising keywords appearing in job postings, local CV norms, and salary context. The Skills Recency card flags skills that are declining in job postings (strikethrough, amber) and highlights skills in high current demand (green). The Career Trajectory card reads your title progression and tells you whether you're on an upward, lateral, or transitional path. The Competitive Keyword Gap card shows the percentage of top-quartile keywords you're covering and lists the highest-frequency ones you're missing. The ATS System card appears when we detect from your job description which ATS the company uses, and tailors parsing advice to that specific system.

resumeTimelineAnalysis.title: Employment gap and short tenure detection
resumeTimelineAnalysis.description: The scanner now parses the date ranges in your work history to detect employment gaps longer than 6 months and roles shorter than 12 months — both of which get flagged by many ATS systems and recruiter screening tools. If gaps or short tenures are found, a new card appears in your results with the specific gap duration, which role it followed, and concrete advice on how to address it (adding a consulting entry, a brief explanation in your summary, or contract role context). Total experience and average tenure are also surfaced.

gatedKeywordGap.title: Top keywords now sorted by how often they actually appear in job postings
gatedKeywordGap.description: Missing keywords in your scan are now ranked by how frequently they appear in real job postings for your role — so the most impactful gaps always appear first. The top 3 are shown in full. Additional high-priority keywords (those appearing in 50–80% of postings for your level) are shown as a blurred preview with a count, so you can see there's more without getting the full list for free.

phraseAwareKeywordMatching.title: Fewer false 'missing keyword' reports
phraseAwareKeywordMatching.description: The keyword gap detector now understands compound phrases, abbreviations, and spacing variants. 'Machine learning' and 'ML' are treated as the same keyword. 'CI/CD', 'ci-cd', and 'cicd' all match. 'P&L' matches 'profit and loss'. 'Full-stack', 'full stack', and 'fullstack' are equivalent. This eliminates a whole class of false positives where a skill you clearly had was being reported as missing because it was written slightly differently.

roleLockDetection.title: Role-specific detection for 50+ job titles
roleLockDetection.description: Added a role-lock system that recognises over 50 unambiguous job titles and forces the correct industry classification regardless of what else appears on the resume. Covered roles include clinical titles (registered nurse, NP, physician, surgeon, pharmacist, EMT), legal titles (attorney, counsel, paralegal), education (teacher, professor, principal), product management (PM, APM, CPO), data engineering (data pipeline engineer, analytics engineer), ML/AI (ML engineer, applied scientist, LLM engineer), and more. Previously, a nurse with SQL in her skills section could be misclassified as technology — this is now impossible.

linkedInInsights.title: LinkedIn profile analysis — see how you look to recruiters
linkedInInsights.description: Add your LinkedIn profile alongside your resume and get a combined analysis: a LinkedIn score, a breakdown of inconsistencies between your resume and profile, resume highlights that should be on LinkedIn, an improved headline and About section opening you can copy in one click, and specific tips to hit LinkedIn's All-Star ranking.

bulletQualityAnalysis.title: Quick wins now target your actual weak bullets
bulletQualityAnalysis.description: Before calling the AI, the scanner now pre-reads every bullet point and identifies which ones start with weak, passive phrases ("Responsible for", "Helped with", "Assisted in") and which ones have no measurable metric. Those specific bullets are handed directly to the AI — so the rewrite suggestions and quick wins in your report are now based on your actual words, not generic advice.

industryDetectionSweep2.title: Sharper industry detection across 20+ roles
industryDetectionSweep2.description: Second-pass bug sweep of the industry detection engine: removed generic false-positive keywords that caused supply chain, operations, and analytics roles to mis-classify; added 30+ missing role-specific keywords for manufacturing, HR, creative, and consulting; expanded the employer lookup table with 30 new companies (fintech, GenAI, Asian tech, collab tools); lowered the secondary industry threshold so cross-functional roles surface their second industry more reliably; and added 15 new co-occurrence patterns to disambiguate analytics engineers, ML engineers, and product designers.

scanFeedback.title: Tell us if your scan was helpful
scanFeedback.description: A quick thumbs up / thumbs down now appears at the bottom of every free scan. Your responses go directly into our improvement pipeline — we use them to identify which recommendation types are systematically off and fix them in future updates.

sectionAwareAnalysis.title: Smarter section-by-section analysis
sectionAwareAnalysis.description: The free scan now pre-parses your resume into labeled sections (Experience, Education, Skills, etc.) before sending it to the AI. This means advice can target specific sections — "add this keyword to your Skills section" — instead of treating your resume as an undifferentiated block of text.

sparseResumeDetection.title: Better advice for short or sparse resumes
sparseResumeDetection.description: Resumes with fewer than 300 words or 5 bullet points now get expansion-focused advice first — what sections are missing, how to add detail, and how to quantify experience — rather than keyword optimization suggestions that don't apply until there's enough content to work with.

fasterPremiumGeneration.title: Premium resume + cover letter generates twice as fast
fasterPremiumGeneration.description: We parallelised the two AI calls that build your rewritten resume and cover letter so they run simultaneously instead of back-to-back. Most premium packages now complete in 15–25 seconds instead of 30–50 seconds.

employerAwareIndustryDetection.title: Industry detection now recognises your employers
employerAwareIndustryDetection.description: We added a database of ~200 well-known companies so the engine can use your employer history as a direct industry signal — Goldman Sachs, McKinsey, Kaiser Permanente, and hundreds more are now recognised instantly. We also fixed how recently-held jobs are weighted: your current role now counts significantly more than jobs from 5+ years ago, so career changers get correctly classified based on where they are today, not where they started.

scanAiReliability.title: More reliable scans when AI is slow
scanAiReliability.description: Added a 55-second timeout to the primary AI call during resume scanning. If the first AI model stalls, the engine now automatically switches to a faster backup model instead of hanging for up to 2.5 minutes. Most users won't notice — but if you've ever seen the scan spinner run unusually long, this fixes that.

industryDetectionAccuracy.title: Sharper, more accurate industry detection
industryDetectionAccuracy.description: We overhauled how we identify your industry from your resume. Six rounds of testing and fixes corrected misclassifications for roles like Growth Hacker (was incorrectly scoring as Data Science), Salesforce Administrator (was scoring as Sales), Quantitative Researcher at a hedge fund (was scoring as Data Science), and Software Engineers working at AI companies (were incorrectly scoring as ML Engineers). We also fixed a scoring logic bug where keyword co-occurrence patterns could fire before any industry signal was established — the main cause of false positives for DevOps engineers and SREs. The result is more accurate industry-specific tips, keyword suggestions, and ATS scoring weights that actually match your role.

dataAiIndustrySplit.title: Data Engineering, Data Science, and AI/ML are now separate industries
dataAiIndustrySplit.description: Previously, data engineers, data scientists, and machine learning engineers all received the same generic feedback under a single 'Technology' category.
